derived: GSK turned 18.02% of revenue into free cash over 2023 to 2025 against the 19.3% its filed expense lines leave. Checked before interest: interest paid is booked under financing, so free cash flow is already struck before interest, so the charge stands. Restated at replacement capex: GSK spent 4,061mm GBP on plant over 2023 to 2025 against 2,628mm GBP of plant depreciation, 1.52% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 1.44% to 0.00%. Restated without one-off cash: GSK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried 1,867mm GBP of legal settlements. None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 21.54% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 23.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -2.23%. It was held at nil, but GSK books 808mm GBP of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001131399-26-000004), 2.47% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -2.23%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 GSK's cash flow statement shows receivables up 1,109mm GBP, inventories up 858mm GBP, payables down 63mm GBP, a working capital build of 2,030mm GBP, 2.15% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -2.23% to -2.47%.

The arithmetic is on the COPD row: Amgen US revenue $567mm, $972mm, $1,478mm and $486mm x4, over a USD 16,912.49 net, 25.37% stopping, and a 644,112 pool depleted by starts. The 0.25x multiple is a judgement, giving 0.02192. Case for: same mechanism as Tezspire at two doses a year instead of thirteen, and Tezspire's US patent runs to 2034-02-03 (Amgen 10-K, data/disclosed_loe.csv), so there is no TSLP biosimilar undercut at launch. Case against: it is the eighth product into severe asthma (Xolair, Nucala, Fasenra, Dupixent, Tezspire, Exdensur from December 2025, tilrekimig from 2030), the second TSLP with no head-to-head data, Exdensur already dosed every six months, and no efficacy disclosed.

column11: GSK 6-K 0001654954-25-006056 (Nucala COPD approval, 22 May 2025): approximately 70% of US COPD patients inadequately controlled on inhaled triple therapy who continue to exacerbate have BEC >=150 cells/uL, over a million people. GSK defines the eosinophilic phenotype on the Nucala label from BEC 150. 1,000,000 / 14,200,000 = 0.070423. PERSIST COPD-1/2 enrol an eosinophilic phenotype with elevated BEC, frequent exacerbations, and triple therapy (or dual if ICS is inappropriate). The trial record does not state the threshold. If it is >=300, the pool falls to about 300,000 (0.0211, the Dupixent label pool cited on tozorakimab's row) and the row would stop pooling with lunsekimig. Leans low, since 'over a million' is a floor.

The CMS new-start series was tried first and refused. Tezspire's Part B plus Part D beneficiaries (3,962, 8,973, 13,837, 21,271 for 2022 to 2025) give new starts of 3,962, 6,016, 7,140 and 10,944. The best logistic has k 0.34, midpoint 11.9 years and an asymptote of 235,824 starts a year (rmse 391, 5.6% of the mean), so the plateau is not identified. The 2022-2024 fit (k 1.22, midpoint -0.05) misses 2025 by 42%, because the 2025 Part D redesign lifted every respiratory biologic's Part D count by 84-87% against 8.6% for Eliquis.
